title: How Sweet and Awful Is the Place
description: How Sweet and Awful Is the Place in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book III, prepared for the Lord's Supper, hymn 13, headed “Divine love making a feast, and calling in the guests, Luke 14. 17 22 23”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How sweet and aw-ful is the place With Christ with-in the doors, While ev-er-last-ing love dis-plays The choic-est of her stores!

lines: How sweet and awful is the place
Here every bowel of our God
Here peace and pardon bought with blood
While all our hearts and all our songs
Each of us cry with thankful tongues,
"Why was I made to hear thy voice,
'Twas the same love that spread the feast,
Else we had still refus'd to taste,
Pity the nations, O our God,
We long to see thy churches full,
May with one voice and heart and soul,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
